classification.difficultyReason: Selects the cosine rule with algebraic adjacent sides, expands and simplifies to a quadratic equation, then rejects the negative root using the positive-length condition.

content.prompt: Find the value of $x$ in the following diagram.

spec.description: Triangle with horizontal base, algebraic side labels and the lower-left 60° angle. Ordinary geometry is black and unshaded.
spec.mathematics: The sides adjacent to 60° are x−3 and x+3; the opposite side is 6√3. No units are supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied labels remain visible; no value of x is shown.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}(6\sqrt{3})^2&=(x-3)^2+(x+3)^2-2(x-3)(x+3)\cos60^\circ\\108&=(x^2-6x+9)+(x^2+6x+9)-(x^2-9)\\108&=x^2+27\\x^2&=81\\x&=\pm9\end{align*}$$

A side length must be positive, so $x-3>0$. Therefore $x=9$.
